extracted.intended_audience: potential subscribers and general readers of a 19th-century home/literary magazine; consumers of advertised goods
extracted.subtask_description: Promotional/editorial guidance and transactional terms for a 19th-century 'Home Magazine' and associated advertised publications/products (what the magazine contains, its editorial standards, subscription/club terms, and product claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Home magazine departmental composition
rubrics_metrics.description: A true 'Home Magazine' must have its TOILETTE and WORK-TABLE DEPARTMENT; its MOTHER'S DEPARTMENT; its HEALTH, CHILDREN'S, and HOUSEKEEPER'S DEPARTMENTS; as well as its strictly LITERARY DEPARTMENT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The aim is to unite the attractions and excellencies of Ladies' (fashion) magazines and literary monthlies, blending the useful with the entertaining so as to please and benefit all classes of readers; excellence is sought in each department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral suitability (editorial policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing is admitted in any way hurtful to morality, honor, or religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit editorial constraint on accepted content across all departments; the magazine positions itself as appropriate for family/home use and favorable in press notices because of that standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary portion quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The literary portion of the HOME MAGAZINE is of the highest character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors contribute largely to the pages and are assisted by liberal contributions from some of the best writers in the country — implying selection for literary merit and reputable contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription pricing, clubbing, and premium rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Yearly terms (in advance) and club rates are specified (e.g., 1 copy $2.00; 2 copies $8.00 for club with premium to getter-up; other multi-copy pricing listed). Premiums are sent to those who make up clubs; three red stamps must be sent in every case to pay the cost of mailing each premium; subscribers to a club need not be at the same post office. Clubbing combinations with other periodicals and their joint prices are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirements for ordering and receiving premiums: payment in advance, specified premium entitlement per subscriber/club, postage-stamp requirement for mailing premiums, and established clubbing offers; orders addressable to publisher or local agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Cyclopædia content scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cyclopædia comprises political, civil, military, and social affairs; public documents; biography; statistics; commerce; finance; literature; science; agriculture; and mechanical industry; political/military events of the U.S. conflict in detail (documents, messages, proclamations, acts, debates, proceedings of states, details of every battle and skirmish involving loss of life), and events connected with privateering, suspension of habeas corpus, martial law, blockade, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It shows political principles with advocates' and opponents' arguments, movements of secession leaders, organization of Confederate States and their regulations, treasury and army organization, and counteracting movements of the United States. It is intended as a comprehensive yearbook of 1861 events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclopædia arrangement, indexing, and physical standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Contents are arranged in alphabetical order and accompanied by a most extensive and complete index; the volume is in the style of the New American Cyclopædia and contains not less than 780 pages, royal octavo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published exclusively by subscription; offered in multiple binding styles (cloth, library leather, half morocco, half russia) with specific prices; local agents appointed to insure uniform price and delivery; payable on delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities required of an effective pulmonary remedy (Ayer's Cherry Pectoral)
rubrics_metrics.description: The indispensable qualities of such a remedy for popular use must be certainty of healthy operation, absence of danger from accidental over-doses, and adaptation to every patient of any age or either sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that these conditions have been realized in the preparation: prepared with chemical accuracy and uniform strength, efficacious in curing pulmonary complaints, widely used (from log cabin to palaces), introduced in foreign countries and used in armies, hospitals, and public institutions; many certificates/testimonials cited as supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities and claims for Ayer's Cathartic Pills
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepared with the utmost skill of the medical profession of the age; cure dangerous complaints quickly and surely; adapted to disease only (produce little effect in health); harmless to tender children; suited to a wide variety of maladies (jaundice, costiveness, headache, neuralgia, gout, worms in infants, rheumatism, dyspepsia, skin eruptions, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed, anecdotal claims of cures are provided as illustrative evidence; advice to take them perseveringly and under the counsel of a good physician if possible — otherwise 'judiciously by such advice as we give you.' The ad emphasizes manufacturing care and specificity (each preparation elaborated to cure one class of diseases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Piano quality attributes (Steinway & Sons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pianos awarded First Premium at the Great World's Fair 1862 for POWER, FULL, CLEAR, BRILLIANT, AND SYMPATHETIC TONE; excellent workmanship shown in grand and square pianos; square piano 'fully possesses the tone of a grand' with ample sound, extension, even tone, sweetness, and power; the grand unites qualities demanded of a concert piano.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims of superiority are supported by extracts from contemporary European musical critics and press (London News of the World, Presse Musicale, Paris Constitutionnel) and by the award at the Exhibition of 1862; warerooms and factory location are given for purchaser evaluation.
